q-54448.name: Question 1
q-54448.worked_solution:
Let's sketch the graph of $y=\operatorname{log}⁡(2-7x).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250624/assets/b4fcf2946431788963444f22bcd51b2a617b53dfc4bbfdd0d8b90bd9fd9304d2.png)

From the graph, we see that the function increases without bound as $x$ decreases. Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\operatorname{log}⁡(2-7x)=\infty 
$$

q-54451.name: Question 2
q-54451.worked_solution:
Let's sketch the graph of $y={log}_{2}⁡(x+4).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250624/assets/57f95a683f7f9c06287bfed1bc459df33dbcdfcdf253d6878e0c77de60d906e0.png)

The function is not defined for $x\le -4.$ Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to -{4}^{-}}{log}_{2}⁡(x+4)=\text{DNE}.
$$

However, the function is defined for $x>-4.$ Moreover,

$$
{lim}_{x\to -{4}^{+}}{log}_{2}⁡(x+4)=-\infty .
$$

Since the left and right-sided limits are not equal, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to -4}{log}_{2}⁡(x+4)=\text{DNE}.
$$
